portion_doctrine: Segments 21-30 of NEXT_INFO_GRABS document are primarily Reddit thread aggregation with boilerplate UI/navigation noise (80-85% junk: ads, upvote counts, Reddit meta, promoted content, navigation elements). Real content emerges from comments on wedding photography pricing, professional photographer income, post-processing philosophy, and fashion/portrait photography methodology. Segment 026 contains video transcript (photographer interview) with timestamps. The extractable gold is thin: pricing discussions, workflow observations, photographer recommendations (Frank Ockenfels, James Minchin, Arnold Newman, Helmut Newton, Yousuf Karsh, Cindy Sherman). No new operating rules, systems, or numbered methods discovered. This portion appears to be raw web-scrape remnants, not curated doctrine.
operating_rules: Post-processing is expected from 'best' photographers but client perception frames the division: retouching (client request) vs post-production (photographer craft mastery). Both are necessary.

Wedding photography budget paradox: $1,500-$3,000 budget gives noticeable quality gaps in candid work; $7,000+ shows fine art background mattering more than price. Quality is differenciated by expertise, not spend.

Professional portrait photographers divide labor: retouching sent to Photoshop specialists (client request); composition/lighting/posing is photographer's core. Capture One recipe applied on shoot day.
Female photographers get booked more for portraiture (gender perception factor mentioned but not explained in this segment set).

Expensive wedding photographers provide: selective curation of best shots (not all raw files), location scouting, pose direction, stress reduction, schedule planning. Budget option provides shoot-only.

contradictions: One thread: 'luxury wedding photography is average photography wrapped in expensive styling' (593 upvotes). Another: expensive photographers deliver fine art with angle/exposure/light play that shows fine art background. Unresolved: is luxury defined by styling or craft?
Pricing debate: 'you get what you pay for' marketing messaging vs actual outcomes where $1k friend shooters deliver 'good enough' memories but $7k delivers art nobody looks at regularly.
